description: The polkit rule that lets the account atoll start the mount units of the pool's disks and refuses it the start of any other mount unit, from the configuration alone: each disk's unit, as systemd-escape --path --suffix=mount names it, in configuration order, a draining disk's included, as the daemon mounts it again after a USB reset; a failed disk's left out, as the daemon never does. In the rule, each unit is a JavaScript string, its backslashes doubled: an escape \x2d left as it is would read '-', and name another unit. The text without --json is the rule, in English whatever the language, so it is the same as the rule of --json.
config:
pool_id = "home-media"
catalog = "${SANDBOX}/catalog.db"
[view]
mount = "${SANDBOX}/pool"
[[disk]]
id = "t1"
uuid = "3f1c9a2e-5b7d-4c1e-9a0b-2d4f6e8a1c3b"
mount = "/mnt/disk1"
fs = "ext4"
[[disk]]
id = "t2"
uuid = "7a2b4c6d-8e0f-4a1b-9c2d-3e4f5a6b7c8d"
mount = "/srv/dev-disk-by-uuid-1234-ABCD"
fs = "ext4"
state = "draining"
[[disk]]
id = "u1"
uuid = "01D9F3A2B4C5E6F7"
mount = "/mnt/Vidéos"
fs = "ntfs"
[[disk]]
id = "t3"
uuid = "9b2e4d6f-1a3c-4e5f-8a7b-6c5d4e3f2a1b"
mount = "/mnt/disk3"
fs = "ext4"
state = "failed"
[[disk]]
id = "t4"
uuid = "5c4d3e2f-1a0b-4c9d-8e7f-6a5b4c3d2e1f"
mount = "/mnt/My Disk"
fs = "xfs"
